text:
sam: heads up — latency and 502s for internal inference traffic in ap-northeast and eu-west starting ~03:33 UTC. quick trace shows failed mTLS resumptions and a pile of KMS AccessDenied entries.

lee: can you paste an example log?

sam: proxy snippet:
```
2026-06-07T03:34:01Z proxy[edge-apn]: tls: session ticket unwrap failed: decrypt error (KMS RequestID: r-0f12c3)
2026-06-07T03:34:01Z proxy[edge-apn]: client=svc-inference, route=/v1/embeds, err="session ticket invalid, rejecting resumption"
```

nora: audit stream shows policy-shipper flipped a keystore role from SHADOW -> ENFORCING at 03:32:58 UTC. The new policy removed kms:Decrypt from the role used by the session-ticket agent.

policy-shipper: audit: PutRolePolicy role=keystore-agent-ap-northeast user=infra-ci mode=ENFORCING change_id=chg-221b

sam: that explains it. the session-ticket unwrap path depends on keystore-agent being able to decrypt the ticket key. without Decrypt we fail earlier than we should and users get 5xx.

lee: immediate mitigation options?

nora: 1) revert the role policy to the last known good (shadow mode) 2) issue a temporary KMS Grant scoped to principal=svc-session-unwrap for 15m 3) enable runtime transient fallback to full handshake in affected region while we repair.

oncall-sre: Creating INC-2026-1921 and adding owners. I'll add a routing rule to divert new sessions away from nodes failing unwrap.

sam: FYI our runtime intentionally rejects fallback to weaker handshakes in global config. we can flip a regional flag to accept a full handshake when unwrap fails, but that relaxes security briefly. propose: accept full handshake for 20 minutes in ap-northeast only while policy revert completes.

lee: i'm rolling the policy revert in ap-northeast now. calling out infra leads to approve.

policy-shipper: deployment:policy-shipper/revert-keystore-apn v2026.06.07-hotfix -> started

auditbot: KMS denies for keystore-agent stop after 03:39:20 UTC in ap-northeast; still failing in eu-west.

sam: after ap-northeast revert error rate dropped to baseline within 3 minutes. eu-west still high; looks like the ENFORCING rollout is partially rolled out there.

nora: action items we should do postmortem: A) Add a preflight keystore unwrap smoke-test to policy-shipper that runs in the target region before switching to ENFORCING. B) Block any non-shadow keystore PutRolePolicy unless security-approved. C) Emit structured proxy audit events when unwrap fails with fields: region, principal, kms_request_id, deny_code. D) Add RBAC-change canary pipeline that applies policy to 1% of identities and runs the smoke-test.

lee: also recommend a short-term change to the runtime: when session ticket unwrap fails due to KMS Deny, the proxy should emit an explicit metric `tls.unwrap.kms_deny` and a tag for region+role. that will make dashboards alert immediately.

sam: longer-term idea: move session-ticket encryption keys into a separate short-lived regional key per cluster with an automated grant lifecycle. keystore policy changes would rarely touch those keys. downside: more keys and grant management complexity.

oncall-sre: added runbook entry "RBAC policy causing KMS denies" with checklist: check audit for PutRolePolicy -> check KMS Deny -> issue emergency grant or revert -> route traffic -> open incident.

nora: I'll open PRs: (1) policy-shipper preflight + fail-safe (owner=infra), (2) proxy structured audit + metric (owner=sam), (3) dashboard alert for tls.unwrap.kms_deny (owner=observability).

sam: Thanks all. Closing INC-2026-1921 as degraded -> recovered after reverts in both regions. We'll include the canary and smoke-test in the next sprint. :thumbsup:
